subject: Climate & Environment
title: How Much Water Earth Really Has
description: One-minute skill: How Much Water Earth Really Has.

hook.text: Earth is 71% water. But 97.5% of it is salty ocean — undrinkable without treatment.

buildup.text: Of the remaining 2.5%, most is locked in glaciers and ice caps, out of reach.

discovery.text: Only 0.3% of all freshwater is in lakes, rivers, and accessible groundwater.

twist.text: All the rivers and lakes on Earth hold less than 1% of freshwater. Most is underground.

climax.text: 8 billion people depend on a fraction of a fraction of Earth's total water.

punchline.text: A blue planet, but almost none of it is drinkable.

quiz.question: What percentage of Earth's water is freshwater?

details.summary: Earth holds about 1.4 billion cubic kilometers of water, but 97.5 percent is saltwater. Of the remaining freshwater, most is locked in ice caps and glaciers. Less than one percent of all water on Earth is accessible liquid freshwater in rivers, lakes, and shallow groundwater.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding how scarce usable water is reframes the crisis. Humanity depends on a tiny fraction of Earth's total water, making conservation and distribution critical.
takeaways: 97.5 percent of Earth's water is salty and undrinkable
Most freshwater is frozen in ice caps and glaciers
Less than one percent is accessible for human use

faq.question: Where is most of Earth's freshwater stored?
faq.answer: About 69 percent of freshwater is locked in glaciers and ice caps, primarily in Antarctica and Greenland. Another 30 percent is groundwater. Surface water in lakes, rivers, and swamps accounts for only about 0.3 percent of all freshwater.

faq.question: Is the amount of freshwater on Earth changing?
faq.answer: The total volume remains roughly constant through the water cycle, but climate change is redistributing it. Glaciers are shrinking, some aquifers are being depleted faster than they recharge, and rainfall patterns are shifting, altering where water is available.
